title: WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry, SharedArrayBuffer, and Atomics are refused: ECMA-262 publishes them and no journal entry can describe what they read
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Determinism-Sensitive Members', rows one and two: 'WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry ... MUST NOT be unconditional globals. deref() returning undefined is a pure function of garbage-collection timing: no capability can mediate it and no journal entry can describe it.' and 'SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics ... MUST NOT be unconditional globals. Cross-agent shared-memory reads and Atomics.wait observe another agent's schedule. That ECMA-262 publishes them is true and irrelevant to replay.' Until 2026-08-28 all four were LISTED in UNIVERSAL_GLOBALS (poc/src/language/semantic.ts) and in the fork's byte-for-byte copy (compiler/forkbridge/hostrules.go.txt), so the allowlist asserted the opposite of the obligation rather than merely failing to meet it: each compiled with zero diagnostics and an empty requirement row on both backends, in the same file where the Date.now() control reported SMITHERS1602. THE CODE IS THE POINT. These are not SMITHERS1601, whose message ends 'access it through a Context capability', because the specification rows say the opposite in as many words -- no capability can mediate these, so naming one would be a remedy that cannot be built. SMITHERS1604 is the precedent: dynamic code evaluation gets its own code for the same 'there is no capability that could provide this' argument. Unlike SMITHERS1604 the line here is the NAME rather than the operation, because every value use of WeakRef is construction and every member of Atomics is a shared-memory operation, so there is no safe read to preserve; the two directions a by-name rule can get wrong are pinned by 20-host-globals/determinism-hostile-siblings-stay-available and by poc/src/language/host-global-allowlist.test.ts, which keeps a type annotation and a lexical shadow legal. Rows three, four, and five of the same specification table -- Promise.race/any charging Scheduler, Date instance members charging Clock, and Intl/localeCompare charging Locale -- remain unenforced and are recorded as (SA-4); each needs a requirement kind that does not exist, which is why they did not move with these two.
